summary_en.motivation: Investigate the impact of laser powder bed fusion process parameters on vertical surface roughness and hardness of thin-walled AlSi10Mg structures.
summary_en.method: Fabricated thin walls with varied process parameters and characterized surface roughness using profilometry and hardness via microindentation.
summary_en.result: Process parameter optimization significantly improved vertical roughness and hardness, with energy density as a key factor.
summary_en.validation: Mechanical testing (hardness) and surface roughness measurements were performed to validate the effects of process parameters.

summary_en.motivation: To develop a crack-free Al-Cu-Mg alloy suitable for selective laser melting by titanium modification.
summary_en.method: Ti addition combined with optimized SLM process parameters to suppress hot cracking.
summary_en.result: The Ti-modified alloy exhibited crack-free microstructure and improved mechanical properties.
summary_en.validation: Microstructural characterization and mechanical testing (tensile/hardness) confirmed crack elimination and property enhancement.

papers.title: Comparison of the biodegradation of ZK30 subjected to solid solution treating and selective laser melting
papers.abstract: This work studied the biodegradation of ZK30 subjected to solid solution treating (SST) and selective laser melting (SLM). The microstructure of SSTed ZK30 was homogenous and consisted largely of the single α-Mg matrix. The microstructure of SLMed ZK30 consisted of fine α-Mg grains containing noncontinuous MgZn2 particles. The biodegradation rates of the SSTed ZK30 and the SLMed ZK30 were lower than that of the as-cast ZK30. The SST and the SLM decreased the biodegradation rate through the elimination of the second phase particles and the refinement of the grain size, respectively. Furthermore, the SLMed ZK30 had a lower corrosion rate.

summary_en.motivation: To compare the biodegradation behavior of ZK30 magnesium alloy processed by solid solution treating and selective laser melting.
summary_en.method: Microstructural characterization and immersion corrosion tests were conducted.

summary_en.validation: Validation via in vitro immersion corrosion testing.

papers.title: In Vitro Corrosion Resistance and Antibacterial Performance of Novel Fe–xCu Biomedical Alloys Prepared by Selective Laser Melting
papers.abstract: Antibacterial Fe– x Cu biomedical alloys are designed to have a satisfactory biodegradation rate compared with pure iron. Fe– x Cu ( x = 0, 1.5, 2.3, 7.8, and 10.1 wt%) alloys are produced by selective laser melting (SLM). Alloying with Cu has a signiﬁcant influence on the grain size, hardness, biodegradation rate, and antibacterial performance of SLMed Fe– x Cu alloys. Increasing Cu content decreases the grain size and increases the hardness. SLMed Fe–1.5Cu, Fe–2.3Cu, and Fe–10.1Cu have degradation rates similar to that of pure iron, while the degradation rate of SLMed Fe–7.8Cu is almost 2.5 times faster. The SLMed Fe–2.3Cu, Fe–7.8Cu, and Fe–10.1Cu produce strong antibacterial performance. The mechanisms of degradation behavior and antibacterial performance are clarified. SLMed Fe–7.8Cu had appropriate mechanical properties, satisfactory degradation rates, strong antibacterial performance, and good cytocompatibility, and therefore is a novel type of antibacterial biomedical alloy with good potential for clinical application.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究SLM制备的Fe-Cu合金的抗菌和腐蚀性能，不涉及多孔结构、应力遮挡或疲劳性能，与用户的研究方向关联性弱。
llm.why_not_core: This paper does not cover porous structure design for stiffness matching, fatigue testing, or osseointegration relevant to implant biomechanics.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发具有可控降解速率和抗菌性能的铁基生物医用合金。
summary_zh.method: 采用选择性激光熔化制备不同Cu含量的Fe-Cu合金。
summary_zh.result: Fe-7.8Cu合金具有合适的力学性能、快速降解和强抗菌效果。
summary_zh.validation: 通过电化学腐蚀、抗菌实验和细胞毒性测试验证性能。

summary_en.motivation: To develop biodegradable Fe-based alloys with controlled degradation rates and antibacterial properties for biomedical applications.
summary_en.method: Fe-Cu alloys with varying Cu content are fabricated via selective laser melting (SLM) to evaluate the effects of alloying on microstructure and properties.
summary_en.result: The Fe-7.8Cu alloy exhibits optimal mechanical properties, a degradation rate 2.5 times faster than pure iron, strong antibacterial performance, and good cytocompatibility.
summary_en.validation: Corrosion resistance is assessed via electrochemical tests, antibacterial performance via plate counting, and biocompatibility via cell viability assays.
